## Design

### 2026-11-01: I started planning out what I wanted there to be on my display. I decided to do a  world clock with a rotary encoder and switches. First, I started building the schematic, using a Raspberry Pi Pico as

**4h**

I started planning out what I wanted there to be on my display. I decided to do a  world clock with a rotary encoder and switches. First, I started building the schematic, using a Raspberry Pi Pico as the microcontroller. I also assigned all of the footprints, and imported all of that into the PCB. Now, I will wire everything and change the layout up so it is put together more nicely. The thing however that took me a lot more time than was necessary was deciding which pins to put CLK and DIO in the microcontroller, since I was confused by the guide saying GP1 instead of what was on there , which was GPIO1.

### 2026-11-01: I worked on wiring everything for the PCBs and made sure that the layout fit nicely together. I made sure that the USB stub on the Raspberry Pi Pico stuck out of the PCB. I finally added an edge cuts

**3h**

I worked on wiring everything for the PCBs and made sure that the layout fit nicely together. I made sure that the USB stub on the Raspberry Pi Pico stuck out of the PCB. I finally added an edge cuts layer to it, and ran the DRC to make sure that nothing bugged out, which led to everything turning out good. Now, I will start by writing the code for the 7 Segment Display.
